descriptors.description: Assign values to workflow state variables using expressions.

fields.name: variables
fields.description: Variables to set in workflow state. Keys are variable names, values can be literals or expressions. Expressions use ${...} syntax, e.g., "${.a + .b}" or "${now}"

variables.description: Variables to set in workflow state. Keys are variable names, values can be literals or expressions. Expressions use ${...} syntax, e.g., "${.a + .b}" or "${now}"

outputJsonSchema.description: set_vars mutates workflow context directly; it does not produce task output.

yamlExamples:
- initialize:
    set:
      variables:
        status: "pending"
        timestamp: "${ now() }"
        request_id: "${ $context.input.id }"

descriptors.description: Make an HTTP request to an external API endpoint.

fields.name: method
fields.description: HTTP method (GET, POST, PUT, DELETE, PATCH).

fields.name: endpoint
fields.description: HTTP endpoint configuration.

fields.name: headers
fields.description: HTTP headers (optional). Values can contain expressions: "Bearer ${TOKEN}"

fields.name: body
fields.description: Request body (optional). Can be any JSON structure. Supports expressions in string values.

fields.name: timeout_seconds
fields.description: Request timeout in seconds (optional, default: 30).

body.description: Request body (optional). Can be any JSON structure. Supports expressions in string values.

headers.description: HTTP headers (optional). Values can contain expressions: "Bearer ${TOKEN}"

method.description: HTTP method (GET, POST, PUT, DELETE, PATCH).

outputJsonSchema.description: HTTP response including status code, headers, and body.

yamlExamples:
- fetch_data:
    call: http
    with:
      method: "GET"
      endpoint:
        uri: "https://api.example.com/tickets/${ $context.ticket_id }"
      headers:
        Authorization: "Bearer ${ .secrets.API_TOKEN }"
    export:
      as: "${ . }"

descriptors.description: Invoke a gRPC method on an external service.

fields.name: service
fields.description: Fully qualified service name. Example: "com.example.UserService"

fields.name: method
fields.description: Method name to call. Example: "GetUser"

fields.name: request
fields.description: Request message (optional). Can be any JSON structure matching the proto schema. Supports expressions in string values.

request.description: Request message (optional). Can be any JSON structure matching the proto schema. Supports expressions in string values.

yamlExamples:
- call_service:
    call: grpc
    with:
      service: "user.UserService"
      method: "GetUser"
      request:
        user_id: "${ $context.user_id }"
    export:
      as: "${ . }"

descriptors.description: Execute a Temporal activity by name with typed input.

fields.name: activity
fields.description: Activity name to execute. Must match a registered Temporal activity.

fields.name: input
fields.description: Activity input (optional). Can be any JSON structure. Supports expressions in string values.

activity.description: Activity name to execute. Must match a registered Temporal activity.

input.description: Activity input (optional). Can be any JSON structure. Supports expressions in string values.

yamlExamples:
- process_payment:
    call: activity
    with:
      activity: "ProcessPayment"
      input:
        amount: "${ $context.order.total }"
        currency: "USD"
    export:
      as: "${ . }"

descriptors.description: Branch conditionally based on expression evaluation.

fields.name: cases
fields.description: List of switch cases (at least one required). Cases are evaluated in order. First matching case executes. If no "when" is specified, the case acts as default.

cases.description: List of switch cases (at least one required). Cases are evaluated in order. First matching case executes. If no "when" is specified, the case acts as default.

outputJsonSchema.description: switch_case directs flow control; it does not produce task output.

yamlExamples:
- route_by_severity:
    switch:
      cases:
        - name: critical
          when: "${ $context.triage.severity == 'critical' }"
          then: escalate
        - name: high
          when: "${ $context.triage.severity == 'high' }"
          then: notify_team
        - name: default
          then: log_and_close

descriptors.description: Iterate over a collection, executing tasks for each item.

fields.name: each
fields.description: Variable name for each item in the iteration. Accessible via ${ $data.item } in expressions.

fields.name: in
fields.description: Expression evaluating to the collection to iterate over. Example: "${ $data.items }" or "${ [1, 2, 3] }"

fields.name: do
fields.description: Tasks to execute for each iteration. Loop variables available: ${ $data.item }, ${ $data.index }

do.description: Tasks to execute for each iteration. Loop variables available: ${ $data.item }, ${ $data.index }

each.description: Variable name for each item in the iteration. Accessible via ${ $data.item } in expressions.

in.description: Expression evaluating to the collection to iterate over. Example: "${ $data.items }" or "${ [1, 2, 3] }"

yamlExamples:
- process_items:
    for:
      each: item
      in: "${ $context.items }"
      do:
        - classify_item:
            call: llm
            with:
              model: "gpt-4o-mini"
              prompt: "Classify: ${ $item.description }"

descriptors.description: Execute multiple branches in parallel, optionally racing.

fields.name: branches
fields.description: Branches to execute in parallel (at least 2 required).

fields.name: compete
fields.description: If true, first branch to complete wins (race mode). If false, all branches must complete (default).

branches.description: Branches to execute in parallel (at least 2 required).

compete.description: If true, first branch to complete wins (race mode). If false, all branches must complete (default).

outputJsonSchema.description: Combined results from all branches (or winner if compete=true).

yamlExamples:
- parallel_enrichment:
    fork:
      branches:
        - name: fetch_profile
          do:
            - get_profile:
                call: http
                with:
                  method: "GET"
                  endpoint:
                    uri: "https://api.example.com/users/${ $context.user_id }"
        - name: fetch_history
          do:
            - get_history:
                call: http
                with:
                  method: "GET"
                  endpoint:
                    uri: "https://api.example.com/history/${ $context.user_id }"
      compete: false

descriptors.description: Handle errors from a block of tasks with recovery logic.

fields.name: try
fields.description: Tasks to attempt (at least one required). If any task fails, execution jumps to catch block.

fields.name: catch
fields.description: Catch block for error handling (optional). If not provided, errors propagate to parent.

catch.description: Catch block for error handling (optional). If not provided, errors propagate to parent.

try.description: Tasks to attempt (at least one required). If any task fails, execution jumps to catch block.

outputJsonSchema.description: Output from the try block (success) or catch block (recovery).

yamlExamples:
- safe_api_call:
    try:
      - risky_call:
          call: http
          with:
            method: "POST"
            endpoint:
              uri: "https://api.unreliable.com/submit"
    catch:
      as: error
      do:
        - log_failure:
            set:
              variables:
                error_message: "${ $error.message }"

descriptors.description: Wait for external signals or events before proceeding.

fields.name: to
fields.description: Signal listening configuration.

outputJsonSchema.description: Signal payload received from the external source.

yamlExamples:
- wait_for_approval:
    listen:
      to:
        mode: "one"
        signals:
          - id: "approval_signal"
            type: "signal"
    export:
      as: "${ . }"

descriptors.description: Pause execution for a specified duration.

fields.name: duration
fields.description: Relative duration to wait from now. Use this when you want to wait for a specific amount of time regardless of when the workflow reaches this task. Example: { days: 7 } = wait 1 week from now

fields.name: until
fields.description: Absolute timestamp to wait until. Use this when you want to wait until a specific point in time. If the timestamp is in the past, the task completes immediately. Example: "2026-03-01T09:00:00Z" = wait until March 1st, 2026 at 9am UTC

duration.description: Relative duration to wait from now. Use this when you want to wait for a specific amount of time regardless of when the workflow reaches this task. Example: { days: 7 } = wait 1 week from now

until.description: Absolute timestamp to wait until. Use this when you want to wait until a specific point in time. If the timestamp is in the past, the task completes immediately. Example: "2026-03-01T09:00:00Z" = wait until March 1st, 2026 at 9am UTC

outputJsonSchema.description: wait does not produce task output.

descriptors.description: Raise an error to terminate execution or trigger error handling.

fields.name: error
fields.description: Error type/name.

fields.name: message
fields.description: Error message. Can contain expressions: "${ .errorMessage }"

outputJsonSchema.description: raise_error terminates the current execution path.

yamlExamples:
- fail_invalid:
    raise:
      error: "ValidationError"
      message: "Required field missing: ${ $context.missing_field }"

descriptors.description: Execute a sub-workflow as a child of the current workflow.

fields.name: workflow
fields.description: Sub-workflow name/identifier to execute.

fields.name: input
fields.description: Sub-workflow input (optional). Can be any JSON structure. Supports expressions in string values.

input.description: Sub-workflow input (optional). Can be any JSON structure. Supports expressions in string values.

outputJsonSchema.description: Output from the child workflow execution.

yamlExamples:
- run_enrichment:
    run:
      workflow: "data-enrichment"
      input:
        user_id: "${ $context.user.id }"
        source: "parent_workflow"
    export:
      as: "${ . }"

descriptors.description: Invoke an AI agent for complex, multi-step reasoning with tool access.

fields.name: agent
fields.description: Agent reference in "org/slug" or "slug" format. - "slug" only: uses the workflow's organization - "org/slug": explicit organization reference Examples: "code-reviewer", "stigmer/code-reviewer", "acme/data-analyst" Required field.

fields.name: org
fields.description: Explicit organization for agent resolution. Optional. If empty, the org is parsed from the agent field or defaults to workflow's org. Use this when you need to override the parsed org.

fields.name: message
fields.description: Instructions/prompt to send to the agent. Supports interpolation of workflow variables using JQ expressions. Example: "Analyze this code: ${ $context.fetchCode.body }" Required field.

fields.name: env
fields.description: Runtime environment variables to pass to the agent. Values can be literal strings or JQ expressions that reference workflow context or secrets. Example: {"GITHUB_TOKEN": "${ .secrets.GH_TOKEN }"} Optional.

fields.name: config
fields.description: Execution configuration for the agent invocation. Optional - defaults are applied if not specified.

fields.name: output
fields.description: Structured output contract for this agent call. When set, the workflow runner extracts structured JSON from the agent's final response and validates it against the declared schema. The validated JSON is placed in the task output under the "structured" key, enabling reliable downstream routing via switch_case expressions. When not set, the task output contains the agent's raw text response (backward compatible with existing workflows).

agent.description: Agent reference in "org/slug" or "slug" format. - "slug" only: uses the workflow's organization - "org/slug": explicit organization reference Examples: "code-reviewer", "stigmer/code-reviewer", "acme/data-analyst" Required field.

config.description: Execution configuration for the agent invocation. Optional - defaults are applied if not specified.

env.description: Runtime environment variables to pass to the agent. Values can be literal strings or JQ expressions that reference workflow context or secrets. Example: {"GITHUB_TOKEN": "${ .secrets.GH_TOKEN }"} Optional.

message.description: Instructions/prompt to send to the agent. Supports interpolation of workflow variables using JQ expressions. Example: "Analyze this code: ${ $context.fetchCode.body }" Required field.

org.description: Explicit organization for agent resolution. Optional. If empty, the org is parsed from the agent field or defaults to workflow's org. Use this when you need to override the parsed org.

output.description: Structured output contract for this agent call. When set, the workflow runner extracts structured JSON from the agent's final response and validates it against the declared schema. The validated JSON is placed in the task output under the "structured" key, enabling reliable downstream routing via switch_case expressions. When not set, the task output contains the agent's raw text response (backward compatible with existing workflows).

outputJsonSchema.description: Agent execution result with dual-channel output.

agent_execution_id.description: Execution ID for drill-down into agent trace.

structured.description: Validated JSON output (when output contract is configured).

yamlExamples:
- triage_ticket:
    call: agent
    with:
      agent: "support-triage"
      message: "${ .ticket.description }"
      output:
        schema:
          type: object
          required: [severity, category]
          properties:
            severity:
              type: string
              enum: [low, medium, high, critical]
            category:
              type: string
        on_invalid: ON_INVALID_RETRY
        max_retries: 2
    export:
      as: "${ .structured }"

descriptors.description: Direct LLM call for classification, extraction, scoring, or routing without agent overhead.

fields.name: model
fields.description: Model reference resolved via the Stigmer model registry. Examples: "gpt-4o", "gpt-4o-mini", "claude-sonnet-4-5", "claude-haiku-3-5" Required field.

fields.name: system_prompt
fields.description: System prompt that sets the LLM's role and constraints. Supports ${ } expression interpolation for dynamic system prompts. Optional — omit for tasks where the user prompt is self-contained.

fields.name: prompt
fields.description: User prompt / instruction sent to the LLM. Supports ${ } expression interpolation for injecting workflow context. Example: "Classify this ticket: ${ $context.ticket.description }" Required field.

fields.name: response_schema
fields.description: JSON Schema for structured output. When set, the runner requests structured output from the provider (e.g., OpenAI's response_format, Anthropic's tool_use extraction) and validates the response against this schema. Uses the same google.protobuf.Struct + JSON Schema pattern as AgentCallOutputContract.schema for consistency across the workflow domain. When not set, the task output is the LLM's raw text response.

fields.name: temperature
fields.description: Sampling temperature (0.0 to 2.0). Lower = more deterministic, higher = more creative. Range is 0.0-2.0 to accommodate all major providers (OpenAI supports up to 2.0; others clamp to their supported range at runtime). Optional — uses the provider's default when not set.

fields.name: max_tokens
fields.description: Maximum tokens in the LLM response. Optional — uses the provider's default when not set.

fields.name: timeout
fields.description: Timeout for the LLM call in seconds. Default: 60. Max: 600 (10 minutes). Optional.

fields.name: on_invalid
fields.description: Policy when the LLM response fails schema validation. Only meaningful when response_schema is set; ignored otherwise. Default: ON_INVALID_FAIL (task fails immediately).

fields.name: max_retries
fields.description: Maximum schema-validation retry attempts when on_invalid is ON_INVALID_RETRY. Each retry re-prompts the LLM with the validation errors and expected schema, giving it an opportunity to self-correct. Only meaningful when on_invalid is ON_INVALID_RETRY; ignored otherwise. Default: 1. Valid range: 1-5.

fields.name: fallback_task
fields.description: Target task to branch to when schema validation cannot be resolved. Used in two scenarios: 1. on_invalid is ON_INVALID_RETRY and all retries are exhausted 2. on_invalid is ON_INVALID_FALLBACK (immediate branch, no retry) Must reference a valid task name in the same workflow. When empty and retries are exhausted, the task fails.

fields.name: max_cost_micros
fields.description: Per-task cost cap in micro-USD (1 USD = 1,000,000 micros). When set, the runtime terminates this specific LLM call if its cost exceeds this limit, independent of the workflow-level budget. The runtime checks both: per-task limit first, then workflow remaining budget. Optional — when 0, no per-task cost limit is enforced.

fields.name: max_total_tokens
fields.description: Per-task token cap (input + output tokens combined). When set, the runtime terminates this specific LLM call if total tokens exceed this limit. Complements max_tokens (field 6), which limits only the output token count as a generation parameter. Optional — when 0, no per-task total token limit is enforced.

fallback_task.description: Target task to branch to when schema validation cannot be resolved. Used in two scenarios: 1. on_invalid is ON_INVALID_RETRY and all retries are exhausted 2. on_invalid is ON_INVALID_FALLBACK (immediate branch, no retry) Must reference a valid task name in the same workflow. When empty and retries are exhausted, the task fails.

max_cost_micros.description: Per-task cost cap in micro-USD (1 USD = 1,000,000 micros). When set, the runtime terminates this specific LLM call if its cost exceeds this limit, independent of the workflow-level budget. The runtime checks both: per-task limit first, then workflow remaining budget. Optional — when 0, no per-task cost limit is enforced.

max_retries.description: Maximum schema-validation retry attempts when on_invalid is ON_INVALID_RETRY. Each retry re-prompts the LLM with the validation errors and expected schema, giving it an opportunity to self-correct. Only meaningful when on_invalid is ON_INVALID_RETRY; ignored otherwise. Default: 1. Valid range: 1-5.

max_tokens.description: Maximum tokens in the LLM response. Optional — uses the provider's default when not set.

max_total_tokens.description: Per-task token cap (input + output tokens combined). When set, the runtime terminates this specific LLM call if total tokens exceed this limit. Complements max_tokens (field 6), which limits only the output token count as a generation parameter. Optional — when 0, no per-task total token limit is enforced.

model.description: Model reference resolved via the Stigmer model registry. Examples: "gpt-4o", "gpt-4o-mini", "claude-sonnet-4-5", "claude-haiku-3-5" Required field.

on_invalid.description: Policy when the LLM response fails schema validation. Only meaningful when response_schema is set; ignored otherwise. Default: ON_INVALID_FAIL (task fails immediately).

prompt.description: User prompt / instruction sent to the LLM. Supports ${ } expression interpolation for injecting workflow context. Example: "Classify this ticket: ${ $context.ticket.description }" Required field.

response_schema.description: JSON Schema for structured output. When set, the runner requests structured output from the provider (e.g., OpenAI's response_format, Anthropic's tool_use extraction) and validates the response against this schema. Uses the same google.protobuf.Struct + JSON Schema pattern as AgentCallOutputContract.schema for consistency across the workflow domain. When not set, the task output is the LLM's raw text response.

system_prompt.description: System prompt that sets the LLM's role and constraints. Supports ${ } expression interpolation for dynamic system prompts. Optional — omit for tasks where the user prompt is self-contained.

temperature.description: Sampling temperature (0.0 to 2.0). Lower = more deterministic, higher = more creative. Range is 0.0-2.0 to accommodate all major providers (OpenAI supports up to 2.0; others clamp to their supported range at runtime). Optional — uses the provider's default when not set.

timeout.description: Timeout for the LLM call in seconds. Default: 60. Max: 600 (10 minutes). Optional.

outputJsonSchema.description: LLM response — structured JSON if response_schema is set, raw text otherwise.

structured.description: Validated JSON output (when response_schema is configured).

text.description: Raw text response from the LLM.

yamlExamples:
- classify_severity:
    call: llm
    with:
      model: "gpt-4o-mini"
      system_prompt: "You are a support ticket classifier."
      prompt: "Classify this ticket: ${ $context.ticket.description }"
      response_schema:
        type: object
        required: [severity, category]
        properties:
          severity:
            type: string
            enum: [low, medium, high, critical]
          category:
            type: string
      on_invalid: ON_INVALID_RETRY
      max_retries: 2
    export:
      as: "${ . }"
- summarize:
    call: llm
    with:
      model: "claude-sonnet-4-5"
      prompt: "Summarize in 2 sentences: ${ $context.document.text }"
      temperature: 0.3
      max_tokens: 200
    export:
      as: "${ . }"

descriptors.description: Deterministic data transformation using JQ, JSONata, or template engines.

fields.name: engine
fields.description: Transformation engine to use. Required — must be explicitly set (not UNSPECIFIED).

fields.name: expression
fields.description: Transformation expression in the chosen engine's syntax. For JQ: a JQ filter expression (e.g., '{name: .full_name}') For JSONata: a JSONata expression (e.g., '{"name": full_name}') For TEMPLATE: a Go text/template string with {{ }} placeholders Required field.

fields.name: input
fields.description: Expression selecting the input data for the transformation. Supports ${ } expression interpolation. When omitted, the entire workflow context is used as input. Example: "${ $context.triage }" to transform just the triage output.

engine.description: Transformation engine to use. Required — must be explicitly set (not UNSPECIFIED).

expression.description: Transformation expression in the chosen engine's syntax. For JQ: a JQ filter expression (e.g., '{name: .full_name}') For JSONata: a JSONata expression (e.g., '{"name": full_name}') For TEMPLATE: a Go text/template string with {{ }} placeholders Required field.

input.description: Expression selecting the input data for the transformation. Supports ${ } expression interpolation. When omitted, the entire workflow context is used as input. Example: "${ $context.triage }" to transform just the triage output.

outputJsonSchema.description: Result of applying the transformation expression to the input data.

yamlExamples:
- build_api_payload:
    transform:
      engine: jq
      expression: '{name: .customer.full_name, severity: .triage.severity, summary: .agent_analysis.structured.summary}'
      input: "${ $context }"
    export:
      as: "${ . }"
- render_message:
    transform:
      engine: template
      expression: "Ticket {{ .ticket_id }} classified as {{ .severity }}"
      input: "${ $context.build_api_payload }"
    export:
      as: "${ . }"

descriptors.description: Workflow-level approval gate that pauses execution for human review or input.

fields.name: prompt
fields.description: Message shown to the reviewer explaining what needs approval or input. Supports ${ } expression interpolation for injecting workflow context. Example: "Approve escalation for ticket ${ $context.ticket.id }?"

fields.name: form_schema
fields.description: JSON Schema defining the input form rendered to the reviewer. When set, the approval UI renders a typed form based on this schema. The reviewer's form response is validated against the schema before the task completes, and the validated data appears in the task output under the "form_data" key. When not set, the reviewer sees only the outcome buttons (approve/deny or custom outcomes) without a data entry form. Uses the same google.protobuf.Struct + JSON Schema pattern as AgentCallOutputContract.schema and LlmCallTaskConfig.response_schema.

fields.name: outcomes
fields.description: Named outcomes that the reviewer can select. Each outcome represents a decision the reviewer can make, with optional routing to a different downstream task. This enables rich branching beyond binary approve/deny. When empty, the task defaults to binary behavior: - "approve": task completes, workflow continues to next task - "deny": task fails (enters try_catch or EXECUTION_FAILED) When custom outcomes are defined, the first outcome is used as the default for HUMAN_INPUT_TIMEOUT_APPROVE, and the last outcome is used as the default for HUMAN_INPUT_TIMEOUT_DENY.

fields.name: approvers
fields.description: Approver identifiers — who is allowed to respond to this task. Supports user IDs, team slugs, and role names. Format examples: - "user:jane@acme.com" — specific user - "team:engineering-leads" — any member of the team - "role:content-admin" — any user with the role When empty, any authenticated user can respond. Resolution of these identifiers is a runtime concern (T13).

fields.name: timeout
fields.description: Timeout in seconds before the on_timeout policy applies. Default: 0 (no timeout — the task waits indefinitely). Max: 2592000 (30 days). A timeout of 0 means the workflow will wait until a human responds. For production workflows, setting a timeout with an appropriate on_timeout policy is strongly recommended.

fields.name: on_timeout
fields.description: Policy applied when the timeout expires without a response. Only meaningful when timeout > 0; ignored when timeout is 0. Default: HUMAN_INPUT_TIMEOUT_FAIL (task fails with timeout error).

fields.name: notification_channels
fields.description: Channel identifiers for sending approval request notifications. When the task starts, the runtime sends notifications through these channels to alert potential approvers. Format examples: - "slack:#approvals" — Slack channel - "email:ops@acme.com" — email address - "teams:#incident-response" — Microsoft Teams channel The format and routing of notifications is a runtime concern (T13). The proto carries the identifiers; the runtime resolves them to actual notification providers configured in the workflow instance's environment.

approvers.description: Approver identifiers — who is allowed to respond to this task. Supports user IDs, team slugs, and role names. Format examples: - "user:jane@acme.com" — specific user - "team:engineering-leads" — any member of the team - "role:content-admin" — any user with the role When empty, any authenticated user can respond. Resolution of these identifiers is a runtime concern (T13).

form_schema.description: JSON Schema defining the input form rendered to the reviewer. When set, the approval UI renders a typed form based on this schema. The reviewer's form response is validated against the schema before the task completes, and the validated data appears in the task output under the "form_data" key. When not set, the reviewer sees only the outcome buttons (approve/deny or custom outcomes) without a data entry form. Uses the same google.protobuf.Struct + JSON Schema pattern as AgentCallOutputContract.schema and LlmCallTaskConfig.response_schema.

notification_channels.description: Channel identifiers for sending approval request notifications. When the task starts, the runtime sends notifications through these channels to alert potential approvers. Format examples: - "slack:#approvals" — Slack channel - "email:ops@acme.com" — email address - "teams:#incident-response" — Microsoft Teams channel The format and routing of notifications is a runtime concern (T13). The proto carries the identifiers; the runtime resolves them to actual notification providers configured in the workflow instance's environment.

on_timeout.description: Policy applied when the timeout expires without a response. Only meaningful when timeout > 0; ignored when timeout is 0. Default: HUMAN_INPUT_TIMEOUT_FAIL (task fails with timeout error).

outcomes.description: Named outcomes that the reviewer can select. Each outcome represents a decision the reviewer can make, with optional routing to a different downstream task. This enables rich branching beyond binary approve/deny. When empty, the task defaults to binary behavior: - "approve": task completes, workflow continues to next task - "deny": task fails (enters try_catch or EXECUTION_FAILED) When custom outcomes are defined, the first outcome is used as the default for HUMAN_INPUT_TIMEOUT_APPROVE, and the last outcome is used as the default for HUMAN_INPUT_TIMEOUT_DENY.

prompt.description: Message shown to the reviewer explaining what needs approval or input. Supports ${ } expression interpolation for injecting workflow context. Example: "Approve escalation for ticket ${ $context.ticket.id }?"

timeout.description: Timeout in seconds before the on_timeout policy applies. Default: 0 (no timeout — the task waits indefinitely). Max: 2592000 (30 days). A timeout of 0 means the workflow will wait until a human responds. For production workflows, setting a timeout with an appropriate on_timeout policy is strongly recommended.

outputJsonSchema.description: Reviewer response including selected outcome and form data.

form_data.description: Validated form response (when form_schema is configured).

reviewer.description: Identity of the user who responded.

yamlExamples:
- manager_approval:
    human_input:
      prompt: "Approve escalation for ${ $context.triage.severity } incident?"
      form_schema:
        type: object
        properties:
          notes:
            type: string
            description: "Optional notes for the engineering team"
          priority_override:
            type: string
            enum: [P1, P2, P3]
      outcomes:
        - name: approve
          label: "Approve Escalation"
        - name: deny
          label: "Reject"
          then: re_classify
      approvers:
        - "team:engineering-leads"
      timeout: 86400
      on_timeout: HUMAN_INPUT_TIMEOUT_ESCALATE
      notification_channels:
        - "slack:#incident-approvals"
    export:
      as: "${ . }"

descriptors.description: Schema and business-rule validation checkpoint for workflow data.

fields.name: input
fields.description: Expression selecting the data to validate. Supports ${ } expression interpolation. Example: "${ $context.triage }" to validate the triage task's output.

fields.name: schema
fields.description: JSON Schema to validate the input data against. Standard JSON Schema (draft 2020-12 or compatible). The runtime validates the input data against this schema and reports detailed errors for any constraint violations. Uses the same google.protobuf.Struct + JSON Schema pattern as AgentCallOutputContract.schema, LlmCallTaskConfig.response_schema, and HumanInputTaskConfig.form_schema. At least one of schema or rules must be set.

fields.name: rules

fields.name: fallback_task
fields.description: Target task to branch to when on_fail is VALIDATION_FAIL_BRANCH. Must reference a valid task name in the same workflow. Only meaningful when on_fail is VALIDATION_FAIL_BRANCH; ignored otherwise. When on_fail is BRANCH and fallback_task is empty, the task fails.

The runtime validates the input data against this schema and reports detailed errors for any constraint violations. Uses the same google.protobuf.Struct + JSON Schema pattern as AgentCallOutputContract.schema, LlmCallTaskConfig.response_schema, and HumanInputTaskConfig.form_schema. yamlExamples:
- check_triage_quality:
    validate:
      input: "${ $context.triage }"
      schema:
        type: object
        required: [severity, category, customer_impact]
        properties:
          severity:
            type: string
            enum: [low, medium, high, critical]
          category:
            type: string
            minLength: 1
          customer_impact:
            type: boolean
      rules:
        - name: critical_needs_rationale
          expression: "${ .severity != 'critical' || (.rationale != null && .rationale != '') }"
          message: "Critical severity requires a rationale"
      on_fail: VALIDATION_FAIL_BRANCH
      fallback_task: human_review

      as: "${ . }"

descriptors.description: Send a notification to humans through a channel (Slack, email, Discord, etc.).

fields.name: channel
fields.description: Notification channel identifier. Determines which notification provider processes this message. Common values: "slack", "email", "discord", "teams", "webhook" This is a string (not an enum) for extensibility — new channels can be added without proto changes. The runtime resolves the channel to its configured provider in the workflow instance's environment.

fields.name: recipients
fields.description: Recipient identifiers for the notification. - alert_slack:
    notification:
      channel: "slack"
      recipients:
        - "#incident-response"
